To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
multilateral R&D alliances are more likely to achieve desired innovation outcomes when the equity governance structure of the alliance is balanced and the alliance has a broad technology scope.
Equity governance and having a multi-technology scope are positively related innovation output in multilateral R&D alliances.
Multilateral alliances are more effective when the equity governance structure is more balanced among the partners and when there is a multi-technology scope among the alliance partners.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of equity governance and multi-technology alliance scope in multilateral R&D alliances and the impact these factors have on alliance performance.
the governance structure and scope of R&D alliances.
the mechanisms that encourage cooperative behavior in multilateral R&D alliances and the impact of these mechanisms on innovation outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of a multilateral alliance is a viable option to achieve innovation outcomes.
multilateral alliances with a high equity share and a multi-technology scope are associated with higher alliance output in terms of innovation outcomes.
the more equity a firm holds, the more likely it is to have successful multilateral alliances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
equity governance and multi-technology alliance scope are both important for the success of multilateral alliances.

equity governance structure and technological scope are important factors in multilateral alliance formation and that firms should be cognizant of the importance of these factors when entering into multilateral alliances.
firms should consider the equity structure and technological scope of their alliances in order to improve the innovation output of their alliance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of R&D multilateral alliances should not be seen as the simple addition of partners to a bilateral alliance.
firms can increase their innovation output by forming a multilateral alliance that is structured around equity governance and has a multi-technology scope.

firms should be aware of these two factors when forming multilateral alliances and should be careful to balance the benefits of cooperation with the costs associated with the complexity of multilateral relationships.
